title: Lesson 30. Final project
description: Finish your game and show it to your parents

questions.prompt: Put the game talk in order
Match the game part with what it does
questions.explain: The whole game from the course.
Also: music, rules, an enemy, a title.

questions.prompt: After the course you not only play games, you create them.
questions.explain: The main result of the course.

questions.prompt: What comes next after the course?
options: Bigger Scratch projects, then HTML and CSS
questions.explain: Mazes, races, quizzes — and the web.
Like our game — up to 10 points.

questions.prompt: In the final project the teacher does everything for the student.
questions.explain: The teacher hints; the student holds the mouse.

questions.prompt: How do you explain what counts the points?
questions.explain: A variable is a box with a number.

learn.intro: The last lesson of the course! You went from "what is a folder" to your very own game!

slides.text: Pick 2–3 improvements: background and music; a rules sign ("Collect 10 apples!"); a second level; an enemy; your game title on the stage.
The teacher only gives hints — **you hold the mouse**.

check.prompt: Who holds the mouse while finishing the game?
check.explain: The main rule of the course.

slides.text: Prepare a talk: 1) the game name and hero; 2) how to play — which keys and what goal; 3) how it works.
"Here is the **if — then** block — it checks whether the hero touched the apple. And here is the **variable** — it counts points."

check.prompt: In the game talk we explain how it works inside.

slides.text: Show your parents: talk about the game, let them play, and show your folder with all your course work: texts, the card, drawings, the presentation, games.
You learned to use a computer and made your first game. Now you don't just play games — **you create them!**

check.prompt: Besides the game, what do we show parents?
options: Your folder with all your work
